archetypes.pitch: Count your basic land types, then cash them in. Ten typed duals and Thran Portal fill out all five, turning Leyline Binding into a one-mana answer and Herd Migration into an entire board. For players who love ramping into powerful, splashy value.
archetypes.rationale: Payoffs at every rarity scale with basic land types while ten typed taplands, Thran Portal and Timeless Lotus provide the fixing.

archetypes.pitch: Start small, finish enormous. Kicker and X-cost spells like Shivan Devastator scale with every land you untap, and Volshe Tideturner helps pay for all of it. For players who like a card that is a turn-two play and a turn-eight finisher.
archetypes.rationale: 50 kicker/X cards reward extra mana; any-color ramp and Volshe Tideturner's kicked-spell mana fund the payoffs.

archetypes.pitch: Dying creatures are the point here, not the cost. Braids, Arisen Nightmare and Nemata, Primeval Warden pay you for every sacrifice while cheap recursive bodies keep the engine fed. For players who enjoy trading, draining and outlasting the opponent.
archetypes.rationale: Death payoffs, sacrifice outlets and recursive fodder all have real depth; Tyrannical Pitlord and Defiler of Flesh join on oracle text.

archetypes.pitch: A wide board, and then two lords to make it lethal. Valiant Veteran and King Darien XLVIII sit on top of token-makers in every colour and turn a modest army into an explosive attack. For players who like flooding the board and swinging as a team.
archetypes.rationale: Soldier-token makers in five colors feed lords and width payoffs; enlist creatures want the same spare bodies.

archetypes.pitch: Cheap spells cast in the right order, until the team is suddenly lethal. Balmor, Battlemage Captain and a squad of Wizards grow and burn as you chain instants and sorceries. For players who love a hyperactive, spell-slinging turn.
archetypes.rationale: Five separate instant/sorcery cast triggers plus engine rares; cheap kicker instants double as spell count.

archetypes.pitch: Your graveyard is a discount, not a dumping ground. Tolarian Terror and Haughty Djinn get cheaper and bigger with every spell that lands in it, while you interact all the way there. For players who like efficient answers backed by a growing bin.
archetypes.rationale: Payoffs count instants/sorceries or creatures in the graveyard while genuine mill enablers fill it.

archetypes.pitch: Permanent counters on a board that only ever grows. Defiler of Vigor pumps every green creature you cast and the kicked payoffs keep stacking more on top. For players who like a steady beatdown that never has to slow down.
archetypes.rationale: Defiler of Vigor mass-pumps every green permanent spell; kicked counter creatures and counter tricks stack the rest.

archetypes.pitch: Answer everything, then win with a single card. Temporary Lockdown and Drag to the Bottom reset the board before Sheoldred or another bomb quietly takes it over. For players who like saying no and winning late.
archetypes.rationale: Real sweepers, taxing pieces, instant-speed draw and clean finishers make classic draft control fully buildable.

archetypes.pitch: Cheap trinkets that quietly add up to an engine. Jhoira, Ageless Innovator and Meria, Scholar of Antiquity draw cards and make mana off the junk you were casting anyway, while Karn, Living Legacy ramps and rewards the density. For players who enjoy value machines built from small parts.
archetypes.rationale: Meria and Jhoira are true engines fed by the cube's cheap nontoken artifact bodies; Karn ramps and pays off density.

archetypes.pitch: Incidental life gain, turned into a real advantage. Shanna, Purifying Blade draws off every point you gain while Sheoldred punishes the opponent for their own draw step. For players who like a steady, resilient grind.
archetypes.rationale: Shanna converts life gained into cards and Knight of Dawn's Light amplifies the cube's abundant incidental gain.

archetypes.pitch: Lands in the graveyard are a resource nobody else is using. Soul of Windgrace and Uurg, Spawn of Turg turn discarded and dead lands back into value and threats. For players who love recursion and grinding out resources.
archetypes.rationale: Soul of Windgrace discards and retrieves lands while Uurg counts them; Serra Paragon replays lands from the graveyard.

archetypes.pitch: Enter-the-battlefield triggers, collected fresh every combat. Golden Argosy mass-blinks your crew to re-trigger cards like Aether Channeler again and again. For players who enjoy chaining ETB value into relentless advantage.
archetypes.rationale: Golden Argosy mass-blinks its crew every combat, re-buying the cube's dense ETB effects.

archetypes.pitch: The biggest tribe in the cube, and it goes wide fast. Leaf-Crowned Visionary pumps and draws off every Elf you cast, backed by mana Elves that get you there a turn early. For players who like snowballing a synergistic creature army.
archetypes.rationale: Sixteen Elves - the largest tribe - behind a lord that pumps and draws off every Elf spell.

archetypes.pitch: Fast red creatures that are perfectly happy to die. Rundvelt Hordemaster is a lord and a death payoff at the same time, and Squee simply keeps coming back for more. For players who want disposable attackers that still generate value.
archetypes.rationale: Hordemaster is lord and death payoff in one; Squee recurs himself; Defiler of Instinct pays off red-permanent density.

archetypes.pitch: A wall of legendary creatures that turns into an engine. Jodah, the Unifier and Ratadrabik of Urborg convert your all-stars into extra bodies and extra cards. For players who like fielding a five-colour legendary lineup.
archetypes.rationale: 48 legendary creatures give Jodah and Ratadrabik constant material, with legend-only mana and equipment as support.

archetypes.pitch: Walls that stop being walls at exactly the wrong moment. Wingmantle Chaplain rewards a board full of defenders and Walking Bulwark lets the fortress get up and attack. For players who enjoy an unconventional plan with a sting in it.
archetypes.rationale: Three payoffs literally count creatures with defender; Walking Bulwark turns the walls into attackers. No rare needed.

archetypes.pitch: The best card in your deck never needs to be cast. The Cruelty of Gix and friends haul premium hits like Archangel of Wrath straight out of the graveyard. For players who love loading the yard and slamming bombs early.
archetypes.rationale: Four true reanimation effects plus mill to stock targets; Archangel of Wrath and Silverback Elder are premium hits.

archetypes.pitch: One creature, properly armed, on a very short clock. Astor, Bearer of Blades tutors up your Equipment and Vehicles and discounts them on the way in. For players who like a lean, weaponised aggro plan.
archetypes.rationale: Astor tutors and discounts the whole package; support is real but shallow, so it is a build-around.

archetypes.pitch: Evasive bodies that pay you for going wide. Vodalian Hexcatcher is a lord and a taxing effect at once, and Defiler of Dreams turns your blue permanents into card draw. For players who like slippery, synergistic beatdown.
archetypes.rationale: Seven Merfolk behind a single lord; Defiler of Dreams turns blue-permanent density into a draw engine.

archetypes.pitch: A tribe that grinds rather than races. Shadow-Rite Priest sacrifices Clerics to tutor up whichever black creature the game needs, backed by steady drain and lifegain. For players who enjoy a tribal aristocrats hybrid.
archetypes.rationale: Eight Clerics behind a lord whose sac ability tutors black creatures; Evolved Sleeper becomes a Cleric on demand.

archetypes.pitch: Flying fatties that refuse to stay in the graveyard. Rivaz of the Claw makes Dragon mana and recasts Dragons straight out of the yard, so the pressure never really stops. For players who want a big, splashy top end.
archetypes.rationale: Rivaz makes dragon mana and recasts Dragons from the graveyard; Shivan Devastator qualifies by its Dragon Hydra type line.

archetypes.pitch: Make everyone throw their hand away, then profit from it. The Raven Man makes a Bird whenever anybody discards, so symmetric wheels and targeted hand attack both pay you. For players who like disruptive, resource-denial strategies.
archetypes.rationale: The Raven Man triggers off any player discarding, so symmetric and self-discard effects all make Birds.

archetypes.pitch: Your removal and your Sagas get up and attack. Zur, Eternal Schemer animates every enchantment you control into a deathtouch-lifelink threat. For players who love a controlling deck with a sneaky enchantment kill.
archetypes.rationale: Zur animates the cube's ten Sagas and removal enchantments into deathtouch-lifelink-hexproof threats sized by mana value.

archetypes.pitch: Every trick you cast happens twice. Ivy, Gleeful Spellthief and Vesuvan Duplimancy copy your single-target spells for two-for-one blowouts. For players who like protecting one threat while piling value on top of it.
archetypes.rationale: Both keystones copy spells that target a single creature you control, turning 14 combat tricks into two-for-ones.

archetypes.pitch: Planeswalkers, protected and then activated twice. Urza Assembles the Titans digs for your walkers and doubles their activations while Plaza of Heroes holds the mana together. For players who love grinding advantage a loyalty point at a time.
archetypes.rationale: The Saga digs for, deploys, and double-activates planeswalkers; five walkers plus Plaza of Heroes support it.

archetypes.pitch: Your big green creatures hit even when they stay home. Enlist taps them to lend their power to an attacker, which pumps Radha, Coalition Warlord on the way, and Keldon Flamesage turns all that borrowed power into free spells. Pick this if you want every creature contributing to every attack.
archetypes.rationale: Enlist turns green's oversized bodies into red's damage; Radha pumps whenever she's tapped - including by her own enlist - and Keldon Flamesage converts enlisted power into free spells.
